items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the election law, in relation to removing binary gender
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6901

SPONSOR: MYRIE
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the election law, in relation to removing binary gender

 
PURPOSE:

To remove binary gender from sections of the election law in relation to
voter information and certain elected positions that require gendered
contests

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends Subdivision 4 of section 2-102 of the election law, as
amended by chapter 373 of the laws of 1978, to provide that designating
petitions and primaries ballots for state committee positions to list
candidates for party positions separately by gender marker, and to allow
for individuals who do not identify as a binary gender to run for state
committee positions that require representation by gender.

Section 2 amends Subdivision 2 of section 2-104 of the election law, as
amended by chapter 234 of the laws of 1976 to provide that designating
petitions and primaries ballots for state committee or convention posi-
tions to list candidates for party positions separately by gender mark-
er, and to allow for individuals who do not identify as a binary gender
to run for state committee or convention positions that require repre-
sentation by individuals of different gender.

Section 3 amends Subdivision 2 of section 2-110 of the election law, as
amended by chapter 373 of the laws of 1978 to allow for assembly
district leader and associate assembly district leader to be of differ-
ent genders, and requires the county committee to establish that allow
for individuals who do not exclusively identify as a binary gender to
serve as district leader.

Section 4 amends Section 2-122 of the election law, as amended by chap-
ter 177 of the laws of 1978 to provide that designating petitions and
primaries ballots for national party delegate and alternate positions to
list candidates for party positions separately by gender marker, and to
allow for individuals who do not exclusively identify as a binary gender
to run for national convention delegate and alternate positions that
require representation by gender.

Section 5 amends Paragraph c of subdivision 3 of section 5-504 of the
election law, as amended by chapter 659 of the laws of 1994 to have
voter information in the state public record list gender rather than
sex.

Section 6 amends Subdivision 7 of section 7-116 of the election law, as
added by chapter 173 of the laws of 2017 to require that where primary
elections in New York City must list candidates separately by gender,
and require such order be decided by lot, separate lotteries shall be
performed for each gender-separated race.

Section 7 gives authority to the state board of elections to promulgate
rules and regulations to provide the ability for individuals who do not

exclusively identify as a binary gender to run for positions elected in
gendered contests.

Section 8 sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Currently, positions that are required to be elected in gender contests
require equal representation by male and female. The way the election
law is currently written, individuals who do not exclusively identify as
a binary gender are not able to run without identifying as a binary
gender. This bill amends several sections of the election law in
relation to gendered contests to better allow for individuals who do not
exclusively identify as a binary gender to be elected to positions
requiring representation and election by gender, and to allow voters to
identify by gender rather than sex on their voter records.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
